reason: Where main/llm/agent/* lives and workspace dependency rules — tool schemas and prompt composition stay in packages/core (Electron-free), dispatch and store access stay in main.
Typed LLM_* error codes, expected-absence-as-state, and the IPC error envelope the existing chat channels return; LLM_AGENT_LIMIT must follow the same append-only convention.
Prompts and chat text are in the never-log class; tool arguments can carry game context and must redact the same way.

Forbidden patterns, A9 meta-test expectations, and mutation coverage for new pure logic (loop step decisions, search filter, tool argument schemas) — the fake LLM must feed the production ChatChunk shapes.
TeacherPanel tool-step rendering conventions: i18n namespace usage, Button primitives, message-list structure the step rows extend.
How the teacher panel consumes streamed chunks today (llm:delta by runId); tool_call/tool_result chunks follow the same store-inputs rule.
M3 wraps M1's wire layer (openai-compatible tool_call accumulation) and M2's engine service — the runner must reuse analyzeOnce-style independent queries, never re-implement framing or engine calls.
Design keeps the IPC surface unchanged; any perceived need to touch ipc.ts is a design violation and must be surfaced, not implemented.
The agent:<n> independent-query contract, 128-visit budget, degrade tri-state, serial tool execution, and the MAX_AGENT_STEPS constant are design decisions the implementation must not drift from.
